# Native freshness timing benchmark

Run through the ordinary Lisa wrapper with Docker available and host Node22.23.3/Bun1.3.8:

```sh
bun run lisa-test-run -- --adapter direct -- python3 tests/fixtures/freshness-native-timing/run.py --source . --output tmp/freshness-native-timing-run
```

The output directory must not exist; its parent must exist. `--expected-head <sha>` additionally binds an assigned Git head. The source checkout must be clean. The launcher requires the wrapper's private TMPDIR and binds the actual Git head plus dispatcher, helper, generated dispatcher and real guard hashes before/after execution. It retains raw output, native traces, event references, tool/image identities and a terminal receipt. The benchmark fails on missing prerequisites, capture ambiguity, timeout, changed source or incomplete execution. Raw receipts can contain invocation paths and must be reviewed/transformed before public export.

The tools-only image uses an immutable official Node registry digest and installs Python3, strace, procps, jq and exact Bun1.3.8. Each run owns a fresh labelled image/container. Immutable image identity plus the ownership label gates cleanup on success and failure; the shared official base is retained. Docker --init supplies the qualified orphan reaper. Source is mounted read-only, container networking is disabled, private executable tmpfs supplies scratch, and ptrace is enabled only in this test container. No application or production dependency is added.

Three actual traced source cases—normal completion, stalled refusal and post-start ps failure—each have a fresh direct twin. Every case must enter its real executable boundary, dispatch all eight genuine guards in order, preserve the original refusal/status, preserve receipt/guard/foreign-sentinel bytes and leave no diagnostic leaf or observed birth-matched survivor before fixture teardown. Native trace and ordinary private guard-name markers cross-check traced execution; direct twins use the same guard markers. No extra file descriptor or production-byte instrumentation is used.

For stalled cases, producer timing starts at the actual anchor fd9 native wait after its own native group qualification and ends at the actual timeout/expiry event. Its conservative measured ceiling is two seconds. Cleanup starts at that expiry and ends at the latest actual anchor reap, first genuine guard exec and observed disappearance of birth-matching diagnostic descendants including zombies. Its conservative ceiling is one additional second. The normal case ends at completion and measures post-completion cleanup; its retained generic `expiry_line` field denotes completion in that case and must not be reported as a timeout. Setup/ps latency and whole guard execution are outside these intervals.

Falsified by: two actual standalone owned native Bash controls feed the same evaluator. A three-second fd9 timeout must be rejected as `producer-expiry-over-two-seconds`; a1.2-second post-expiry delay must be rejected as `expiry-to-reaping-and-guard-over-one-second`. The launcher requires exactly three traced/direct pairs and exactly two controls rejected at their named boundaries. These controls qualify the timing detector; they never mutate production bytes. Missing events or clocks cannot become synthetic passing timestamps.

The original qualified source run used Linux AArch64, Bash5.2.15, strace6.1, Python3.11.2 and jq1.6. Selected image/kernel/tool identities are captured on every run; no AMD64 result is inferred from that local run or the registry reference. The unchanged accepted driver/evaluator are promoted here; the generalized launcher and its committed/hosted execution still require fresh qualification.

`strace -ttt` wall timestamps and native syscall durations are checked against sampled wall-minus-monotonic offsets; their observed range plus timestamp resolution is added to bounds. Sampling gaps are recorded. A birth census can miss short-lived descendants, and clock checks are sampled. Traced/direct whole-call differences include scheduling variance and guard ptrace overhead, so they are not pure diagnostic overhead. No universal clock, scheduler, native ps or uninterruptible-kernel-I/O guarantee is claimed. The separate fifteen-case hosted regression and exact genuinely published-package replay remain distinct obligations.
